recipes.name: Potato Hash Cakes with Baked Marinated Tempeh
instructions: Mix together the soy sauce, maple syrup, and sriracha in a large, shallow bowl.
Add the tempeh to the shallow dish and toss to coat. Let marinate for 20 minutes. Mix once or twice while it's marinating to re-coat.
Line a baking tray and preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C)*.
Grate the potatoes and the onion, then use your hands or a clean kitchen towel to squeeze out any excess liquid. Transfer the grated mixture to a large bowl.
Add the remaining hash cake ingredients (except the cooking oil spray) and mix well.
Use a ½ cup measure to scoop up the potato mixture. Flatten into ½ cm thick cakes on the baking tray.
Place the tomatoes on the tray to bake as well and spray the potato cakes with some oil.
Bake for 35 to 40 minutes, or until the cakes are cooked and golden.
Meanwhile, heat some oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Add the tempeh slices and cook until golden, about 4 minutes per side. Set aside.
Add the spinach to the now-empty pan. Stir often, and once wilted, add the garlic. Cook for 2 to 3 minutes.
To serve, use a potato cake as the base, and top with a few avocado slices, garlicky spinach, baked tempeh, and blistered tomatoes. Enjoy!

page_recipe_notes: Notes † For us, 2 medium potatoes weighed 420 g. † For us, 1 small onion weighed 70 g. * We used top and bottom heating (not fan-assisted/convection).
Storage This dish is best enjoyed freshly made. Store each component separately in its own airtight container for up to 3 days.
